title: Earnest Money Receipt
summary: Acknowledge receipt of an earnest money deposit and state how it will be held and released.
useWhen: A title company, escrow agent, attorney or seller receives the buyer's deposit under a purchase contract.
watchOuts: Licensees and escrow agents must follow state trust-account rules for holding deposits, including deposit deadlines and separate accounts. Sellers holding deposits themselves is risky for buyers.
If there is a dispute, most holders will not release the deposit without joint instructions or a court order. Some states have specific release procedures.
Confirm wiring instructions by phone using a known number. Earnest money wires are a top target for fraud.

variables.label: Escrow holder
variables.help: Title company, attorney, broker or seller holding the deposit.

variables.label: Funds held in
variables.default: a federally insured escrow or trust account

variables.label: Interest-bearing account?
variables.help: If on, say who gets the interest.

variables.label: Interest belongs to
options: the party who receives the deposit

sections.title: 1. Receipt
sections.body: {{holder_name}}, {{holder_address}} ("Holder") acknowledges receiving {{amount}} from {{buyer_name}} ("Buyer") on {{receipt_date}} by {{form}} (reference {{reference}}), as earnest money under the purchase contract dated {{contract_date}} between Buyer and {{seller_name}} ("Seller") for {{property_address}}. Receipt of a check is subject to collection. If a check is dishonored, Holder will notify both parties promptly.

sections.title: 2. Holding the deposit
sections.body: Holder will keep the deposit in {{account_type}}, separate from Holder's own funds, as the law requires.

sections.title: 3. Interest
sections.body: The account bears interest. Interest belongs to {{interest_to}}. Buyer will provide a Form W-9 if requested.

sections.title: 4. Release
sections.body: Holder will release the deposit (a) at closing, as a credit to Buyer, (b) according to joint written instructions signed by Buyer and Seller, (c) as the purchase contract clearly provides after notice to both parties where the law allows, or (d) under a court order. If Buyer and Seller dispute who is entitled to the deposit, Holder may keep it until the dispute is resolved, or deposit it with a court and ask the court to decide (interpleader), as allowed by state law.

sections.title: 5. Holder's role
sections.body: Holder is a stakeholder only, does not represent either party, and is not liable for acting in good faith under this receipt. This receipt does not change the purchase contract.

sections.title: 6. Wire fraud
sections.body: **Wire fraud warning.** Criminals send fake wiring instructions by email that look like they come from title companies, attorneys and agents. Before wiring any money, call the recipient at a phone number you get independently, not from the email, and confirm the instructions. Never trust a last-minute change to wiring instructions.

sections.title: Signatures
sections.body:
Signed by Holder, and acknowledged by Buyer:

**Escrow holder** — {{holder_name}}

[[sig:holder]]

Printed name: [[name:holder]]
Title (if signing for a company): [[text:holder:Title]]
Date: [[date:holder]]

**Buyer** — {{buyer_name}}

[[sig:buyer]]

Printed name: [[name:buyer]]
Date: [[date:buyer]]

disclaimer: This is a starting template from the Massless open contract library. It is not legal advice, and using it does not create an attorney-client relationship. Laws vary by state and change over time. Have a licensed attorney in your state review it before you sign. Real estate contracts carry state-specific disclosure, licensing, closing and recording rules. If a real estate licensee is involved, the licensee may be required to use state-promulgated or approved forms instead of this one (for example in Texas and Colorado). Deeds, mortgages and deeds of trust usually must be notarized and recorded; an electronic signature on this document does not record anything.
